grammar.topic: Week 14 review: reporting verbs, relative clauses, participles, used to, stop/remember/try
explainTr: Bu hafta beş yapı gördün. Aktarma fiilleri: suggest/admit/deny + -ing, advise/warn + kişi + to. Virgüllü cümlecikler: who, which, whose, where (that yok).
Kısaltılmış cümlecikler: students arriving late (etken, -ing), forms submitted late (edilgen, V3). Alışma yapıları: used to + fiil (eskiden), be/get used to + -ing (alışık / alışmak).

Anlamı değişen fiiller: stop to do / stop doing, remember to do / remember doing, try to do / try doing, regret to tell / regret doing. Okul politikası metinlerinde bu yapıların hepsi bir arada gelir.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede bu yapıların çoğu ek ve sıfat-fiillerle kurulur. İngilizcede ise kalıp önemlidir: fiilin yanındaki yapı (to / -ing / that) anlamı ve doğruluğu belirler. Çalışırken önce fiile, sonra kalıba bak.

reading.title: The school policy summary
reading.text:
At the end of the week, Mr. Brown handed Hafsa a two-page summary of the school's attendance and conduct policy. "You do not have to memorize it," he said, "but you should know what to do when something happens." Hafsa took it home and read it slowly with a dictionary.

The first part, titled Attendance, explained that students who are absent must bring a note signed by a parent or guardian within three days. Absences supported by a doctor's note are excused, while others are unexcused. Students arriving after 8:15 are marked tardy, and three tardies in a month result in a letter sent home. The policy, which was revised last spring, clarifies that the front office must notify parents by phone when a child is missing without explanation.

The second part, Conduct, listed the expectations for every student. Children are asked to treat others with respect, to follow directions the first time, and to keep their hands to themselves. Teachers are advised to use positive reinforcement before any consequence. When misbehavior continues, they should talk to the student privately and record the incident in the school system. The principal, who makes the final decision on suspensions, must contact the family before any serious step is taken.

The third part concerned technology and safety. Phones seen during class are taken to the office, and students using school computers must follow the guidelines posted next to each lab. Visitors entering the building sign in and wear a badge. Parents wishing to speak with a teacher should make an appointment rather than stopping to chat during lessons, because teachers need to remember to focus on the children.

A short paragraph at the end explained that the policy is reviewed every year by a committee including teachers, parents, and an administrator. Families can send comments by email, and the committee's recommendations are published on the school's website.

Hafsa highlighted three sentences she wanted to remember. She also wrote a question for Mr. Brown: "Who decides when a student is eligible to join the field trip?" Reading the policy had been a lot of work, but now she felt she could explain it to anyone, in plain English.

script.speaker: Mr. Evans
script.text: Hello, I'm Mr. Evans. My daughter was absent on Monday and Tuesday.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Hello. Do you have a note for the absence?

script.speaker: Mr. Evans
script.text: She had a fever, so I took her to the doctor. Here is the note, signed by the doctor.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Perfect. Absences supported by a doctor's note are excused. May I have her name?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you. I'll notify her teacher, who can send the missed homework home.

script.speaker: Mr. Evans
script.text: That's great. Also, Mia used to ride the bus, but now I'm dropping her off. Where should I park?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Parents dropping off children should use the side lane. Mr. Brown said that the bus zone is not allowed for cars.

script.speaker: Mr. Evans
script.text: Understood. Is there a form for that?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: No form, but please remember to pick her up before three thirty.

script.speaker: Mr. Evans
script.text: I will. Thank you for your help.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: You're welcome. I hope Mia feels better soon.

writing.promptTr: Okul adına velilere bir telefon politikası duyurusu yaz. En az bir aktarma fiili, bir virgüllü cümlecik, bir kısaltılmış cümlecik ve used to / remember to gibi bir yapı kullan. 120-180 kelime yaz.
writing.promptEn: Write a notice to parents about a school phone policy. Use a reporting verb, a non-defining clause, a participle clause, and one more structure from this week.
writing.model: Dear families, the school committee, which met last Tuesday, has reviewed the phone policy. The principal admitted that the old rule was confusing, and she suggested writing a simpler version. From next month, phones brought to school must stay in backpacks during lessons. Devices seen in class will be taken to the office, where parents can pick them up after school. Students using phones for medical reasons should bring a note signed by a doctor. Teachers have been advised to remind students politely before they take any action. I used to think that such rules were too strict, but I have gotten used to the idea that clear limits help children focus. Please remember to read the full policy on our website and to talk about it with your child. If you have questions, the front office, which is open from seven to four, will be glad to help. Thank you for your cooperation and support. Sincerely, Mr. Brown
checklistTr: En az bir aktarma fiili (admit, suggest, advise, warn, deny) var mı?
Kısaltılmış bir cümlecik (-ing veya V3) var mı?
remember to / used to gibi bir yapı kullandın mı?
